recommendation: Keep the source fix unless FHIR-I/FMG explicitly decides that CapabilityStatement messaging and document sections are normative or adopts a different current mechanism for trial-use content inside normative resources.
issue_request: FHIR-14410 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 FHIR-I change request asking whether CapabilityStatement.messaging and CapabilityStatement.document had enough experience to go normative; the accepted resolution said these parts were not ready to go normative and should be marked as such.
initial_application: The issue was applied in migrated svn revisions 13047 and 13048, now git commits 94ddb5e6ea93bcefdd16c33a02bdc60d0fb9129d and c4f5b955188866b4924aa5d7707c411239bf6fe2, which added trial-use status for CapabilityStatement.messaging and CapabilityStatement.document in the spreadsheet sources. The 2021 source migration carried those markers into structuredefinition-CapabilityStatement.xml.
additional_context: CapabilityStatement is active in source/fhir.ini and is a normative conformance resource, so element-level standards-status extensions are the current source mechanism for trial-use parts. Commit 5c20769cc74459a8c1057d2747418dc4340f4244 later removed many CapabilityStatement trial-use markers, including messaging and document; the related FHIR-15646 reconciliation restored another marker removed by the same cleanup. No Jira, Zulip, or Confluence evidence was found that supersedes the specific FHIR-14410 decision.
reconciliation: Added structuredefinition-standards-status extensions with value trial-use to CapabilityStatement.messaging and CapabilityStatement.document in source/capabilitystatement/structuredefinition-CapabilityStatement.xml.
source_changes: source/capabilitystatement/structuredefinition-CapabilityStatement.xml: restored trial-use standards-status extensions on CapabilityStatement.messaging and CapabilityStatement.document.

related_jiras.note: Broader CapabilityStatement normative-status audit noted FHIR-14410 but was limited to rest.resource and /metadata mode guidance, so it did not decide this seed.
Another specific CapabilityStatement section status marker was removed by the same cleanup and restored by reconciliation, supporting the focused element-level marker approach.
Broader R5/R6 status-marking work confirms element-level standards-status extensions are the current source mechanism but does not supersede FHIR-14410.
